p01_wood:
Edo-period Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print in the manner of Utagawa Kuniyoshi's yokai and ghost prints of the 1840s: bold confident black sumi keyblock outlines, flat areas of colour, deep Prussian blue with soft bokashi gradients, muted ochre, sage green and touches of vermilion, cream washi paper texture with visible woodgrain and slight registration offsets, dramatic composition, stylised kasumi mist bands.

Scene: a dark wood at night seen from within: tall trunks, tangled undergrowth and brambles, a sliver of moon behind thin clouds, utter stillness, faint mist between the trees; the tiny glowing eyes of a few hidden yokai (a tanuki, a kitsune, a one-eyed spirit) peek from the shadows. Mostly dark and low-key, mysterious. Wide establishing shot.

No text, no signatures, no seals, no cartouches, no lettering of any kind.
p02_hero:
Edo-period Japanese ukiyo-e woodblock print in the manner of Utagawa Kuniyoshi's yokai and ghost prints of the 1840s: bold confident black sumi keyblock outlines, flat areas of colour, deep Prussian-blue night sky with soft bokashi gradient, muted ochre, sage green and touches of vermilion, cream washi paper texture with visible woodgrain and slight registration offsets, dramatic asymmetric composition, stylised kasumi mist bands.

Scene: night in a European thicket rendered as a Japanese print. A single small common nightingale — a plain warm-brown bird with a rufous tail, pale buff throat and large dark eye — perches on a thorny bramble branch in the lower-left third, beak wide open in full song. Behind it an enormous pale full moon. From its beak unfurl curling ribbons of pale mist that turn into tiny ghostly spirit-wisps, like small yokai made of sound, drifting upward. Dense dark silhouettes of thicket and tree trunks frame the bottom edge. Keep the right half mostly open night sky.

No text, no signatures, no seals, no cartouches, no lettering of any kind.

A long faint dotted trail of the bird's path arcs across the sky from lower right to upper left. A sense of an immense journey for a tiny traveller.
